statement.excerpt: Yet we’re still in the period where “doing AI” feels good and gets rewarded (or not doing AI gets punished), which means the spend will continue until everybody realizes they can likely cut a shit ton of costs, first by moving to open source models, then not using them at all, because even open source is expensive and questionably-useful.

the spend will continue until everybody realizes

our_interpretation: Read as a forecast of a broad enterprise trend, rather than literal unanimity among every enterprise.
The predicted sequence is continued spending, followed by cost-driven migration to open-source models, followed by abandonment of those models.
The condition is an environment that rewards AI adoption. The expected realization about savings is part of the forecast, not an independently satisfied antecedent.
The claim names no company, spending measure, accounting basis, or deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Representative longitudinal records show the stated sequence across enterprises, with cost savings driving migration and subsequent abandonment, while the adoption-reward condition is established.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A completed broad transition following the stated realization decisively takes a different path. Continued spending or isolated counterexamples cannot disprove this undated forecast.
